ROLE: Encode exactly one QoS 0 PUBLISH (DUP 0, RETAIN 0) into the broker scratch buffer and append those bytes to the output queue of every READY session whose subscription matches the topic, including the publisher itself, closing only a recipient whose queue could not grow.

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_encode_publish
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int wire_encode_publish(struct byte_buf *out, const uint8_t *topic, size_t topic_len, const uint8_t *payload, size_t payload_len, uint8_t qos, uint8_t dup, uint8_t retain)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 after appending one complete PUBLISH: fixed header byte 0x30 (DUP 0, QoS 0, RETAIN 0), the Remaining Length encoding of 2 + topic_len + payload_len, the 2-byte big-endian topic length, the topic bytes, then payload_len payload bytes; -1 for a NULL/illegal argument; -2 when the destination could not grow
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: topic and payload are borrowed and copied into out; out keeps ownership of the appended bytes
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: nonzero appends nothing (the buffer is unchanged), so a failed encode produces no message at all and the caller must not close any session for it

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_consume
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the first n bytes are removed by moving the remaining bytes to the front and len is reduced by n (n > len is clamped); the allocated storage is kept
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: storage stays owned by the buffer so the scratch buffer is reused for every publish without repeated allocation
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; buffer_consume(scratch, scratch.len) leaves len == 0 with capacity intact

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_state
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the current lifecycle state; SESSION_CLOSED for NULL

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_matches_topic
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int session_matches_topic(const struct session *s, const char *topic, size_t topic_len)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 1 when any stored filter matches the topic by one level per '/' with '+' and trailing '#' semantics, 0 otherwise (including 0 for NULL or an empty subscription list)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: topic is borrowed for the duration of the call and is never retained or modified

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_enqueue
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int session_enqueue(struct session *s, const void *data, size_t len)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when len bytes were appended to the recipient's queue; -1 on invalid arguments or allocation failure
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the bytes are copied; the session owns the copy and the scratch buffer stays owned by the broker
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 leaves the recipient's previously queued bytes untouched and appends nothing, so the caller closes that one recipient instead of retrying

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_immediately
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the recipient's queued bytes are released, its descriptor is closed once and its state becomes SESSION_CLOSED
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases that recipient's descriptor and queued bytes; the registry slot stays until broker_reap destroys it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a no-op on an already CLOSED session, which keeps the fan-out loop safe

LOGIC.INPUT: b: broker whose sessions array, count and scratch buffer are used. pub: decoded PUBLISH; pub->topic/topic_len and pub->payload/payload_len are borrowed slices into the publishing client's receive buffer and stay valid for the whole call because the caller consumes the frame bytes only after this returns.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. Clear scratch: buffer_consume(&b->scratch, b->scratch.len) so the retained capacity holds exactly the next encoded packet (this releases no storage, it only sets len to 0). 2. rc = wire_encode_publish(&b->scratch, pub->topic, pub->topic_len, pub->payload, pub->payload_len, 0, 0, 0). 3. If rc != 0 (invalid argument or allocation failure) return immediately without closing or modifying any session: a QoS 0 message that cannot be encoded is dropped, and no recipient loses its connection for the broker's own memory failure. 4. n = b->count captured once; for i = 0 .. n-1: t = b->sessions[i]; skip t == NULL; skip session_state(t) != SESSION_READY; skip session_matches_topic(t, (const char *)pub->topic, pub->topic_len) == 0; then if session_enqueue(t, b->scratch.data, b->scratch.len) != 0 call session_close_immediately(t) so only the failing recipient is closed while every later recipient is still visited. The loop never calls broker_reap, so the array is not compacted and index i stays valid; closed recipients stay in their slots with state SESSION_CLOSED until the execution layer reaps them. 5. After the loop, buffer_consume(&b->scratch, b->scratch.len) so the scratch buffer is left empty and ready for reuse.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. On success every READY matching session - including the publisher when its own subscriptions match - has one copy of 30 <RL> <2-byte topic length> <topic> <payload> appended to its queue, in registry order, and the scratch buffer is empty with its storage retained. On an encode failure no session is touched. A recipient whose enqueue failed is SESSION_CLOSED (descriptor closed, queue released) and the remaining recipients are unaffected.
INVARIANTS_USED: one QoS 0 copy per matching READY session, with topic and payload bytes preserved exactly (payload is length-delimited and may contain 0x00, and may be empty)
the publisher receives its own copy when one of its subscriptions matches, because it is an ordinary registry entry
matching is case sensitive and uses MQTT level semantics via session_matches_topic
the registry array is not compacted during fan-out, so a failing recipient cannot invalidate the iteration
error isolation: only the recipient whose queue could not grow is closed
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: b and pub are non-NULL; the caller has already rejected pub->qos != 0; the receive buffer holding pub's slices stays alive until this function returns.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: scratch.len == 0 (intact capacity) and no session other than a failed recipient changed state; each matching READY session's queue grew by exactly the encoded packet length.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; no session is created or destroyed while the fan-out loop runs.
